retrieval: Primary full text: methods, tables, results and relevant discussion read
origin: Food-page phytate-reduction screen followed by new original literature search
population: 10 healthy adults, seven women and three men, 21–30 years

protocol.malting: Dehulled oats steeped 6.5 h at 25 C; germinated 120 h at 15 C under controlled moisture; dried 18 h at 30 C and staged to 80 C.
protocol.soaking: 30 g ground malted oats in 150 mL water; 17 h at 23 C then 8 h at 37.8 C; refrigerated overnight, frozen, thawed and microwave-cooked for 2 min.
protocol.comparator: 30 g untreated dehulled ground oats from the same batch; cooked without milk or jam.
protocol.design: Each participant received both meals in random order; extrinsic 65Zn labelling and whole-body retention at 10–14 days.

outcome: Fractional zinc absorption 18.3% versus 11.8%; paired comparison P<0.05.
pm_relevance: Existing admitted zinc is a catalytic BHMT participant. Absorption evidence supports upstream provision, not increased BHMT activity or homocysteine clearance.
limitations: Pilot-plant malting is not household overnight soaking of commercial oats.
No zinc status, tissue BHMT flux or clinical benefit endpoint.
Iron experiments used different meals and methods; one iron comparison was nonsignificant.
Short-term isotope absorption in ten healthy adults; no universal serving prescription.
disposition: Implemented as PM2-SOP-MALTED-OATS-1: qualified upstream zinc provision; no measured BHMT flux claim
